subject: Post-call: benchmarking methodology & SLOs for EdgeFin integration
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@edgefin.com>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@edgefin.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: benchmarking methodology & SLOs for EdgeFin integration

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared starting point for the SLO/benchmark work.

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference profile against EdgeFin latency & throughput SLOs for the document-summarization endpoint (batch and streaming).
- Key constraints: p95 latency target for typical traffic, predictable tail behavior during bursts, and streaming support for progressive token delivery.

Proposed SLO targets (for discussion):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for responses up to 512 tokens (cold-start excluded); p99 <= 500ms.
- Throughput: sustain 1200 concurrent requests (average request size ~150 tokens) with 95% of requests meeting p95 latency.
- Concurrency: support 1.2k concurrent clients with graceful degradation to a compatible smaller model when saturated.
- Streaming requirements: partial token streaming enabled for any response >64 tokens; initial token (first byte) within 120ms.

Benchmark methodology (proposal summary):
1) Prompt sets: we will use the attached promptset v1 (benchmark-promptset-v1.jsonl). It includes 200 realistic customer prompts sampled from your production telemetry (anonymized) and 50 synthetic edge-cases for long responses.
2) Eval harness: we will run 10 full passes across the promptset for each model variant. Each pass will include:
   - Cold-start run (new worker pool) to capture cold latencies
   - Steady-state run for 30 minutes with configured concurrency profile
   - Burst test with 5x traffic for 2 minutes to evaluate degradation policies
3) Measurement definitions: per-request latency measured from request received to last token delivered; streaming "first-byte" measured separately. Tokenization done with model tokenizer; token counts included in metrics.
4) Reproducibility: full harness + configs will be shared via Drive (see link). We'll version prompt sets and harness configs; results will include raw traces and aggregated summaries.

Next steps / asks from EdgeFin:
- Confirm the SLO targets and any additional constraints (e.g., max cost-per-token target or hard max latency).
- Share any rate-limit or client-side retry behavior we should emulate.
- Approve an initial benchmark window: propose next Tuesday 2026-06-09 09:00-12:00 PT for initial runs.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-proposal.pdf (proposal + run configs), benchmark-promptset-v1.jsonl (prompt samples).

Thanks

Thanks Marissa

is great, and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Concurrency/throughput: can you add a scenario that emulates peak trading-window behavior where concurrency can spike to ~1500 simultaneous short requests (avg 30 tokens) for ~1 minute? We want to ensure the fallback behavior is predictable under short spikes.

2) Cold-start: we have an important constraint that first request after a scale-up must not exceed 800ms at p95 (our users are sensitive to initial delays). Is this something Redwood can target in the cold-start run?

3) Cost cap: our infra team asked for a rough cost estimate for the initial benchmark run (3 passes). If you can include a ballpark number in the proposal PDF or in the shared Drive doc that'd be helpful.

We'll also loop in security/compliance shortly for the evidence pack; Priya will coordinate with your team on required artifacts.

I can confirm the proposed window (Tue 2026-06-09 09:00 PT) Dev, can you confirm infra availability on your side?

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Platform, EdgeFin
